title: Impact of Government’s COVID-19 Financing Schemes on Businesses
what_it_is: Impact of Government’s COVID-19 Financing Schemes on Businesses

sections.label: SME loan applications and approvals
sections.summary: ESG data shows SME borrowers applied for over 2,500 loans worth about S$1.9 billion since March, with 90% to 95% approval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Based on ESG’s data, SME borrowers have applied for more than 2,500 loans amounting to about S$1.9 billion since the beginning of March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The approval rate of these loan applications has been high, at 90% to 95%.

sections.label: ESG loan scheme interest rates
sections.summary: With earlier ESG loan scheme enhancements, interest rates are expected to fall to 2%-3% for most borrowers, versus 6% or more for other unsecured SME working capital loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Together with the earlier enhancements to the ESG loan schemes, this is expected to bring down interest rates for such loans to 2%-3% for most borrowers, compared to 6% or more for most other unsecured working capital loans to SMEs today.

sections.label: Secured loan facilities benefiting
sections.summary: More than S$4.5 billion of secured loan facilities have benefited from this measure to-date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: More than S$4.5 billion of secured loan facilities have benefited from this measure to-date.

sections.label: SME processing times and credit
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government has tracked if ESG loan processing times have come down, given feedback that times remain considerable and some SMEs need credit quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Just two questions for the Minister to follow up on that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, there is still anecdotal feedback that the processing times are still quite considerable and there are some SMEs that are in distress and they need the credit to come in quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, has the Government been tracking whether those processing times for the ESG loans have come down, is it trending in the right direction?

sections.label: Bridging loan processing times and ownership
sections.summary: Processing time data ranges from one to eight days, mostly four to five days, and the question cites companies unable to obtain ESG bridging loans where local shareholding is under 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As to the processing time, I do have some data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It ranges from one to eight days with the majority hovering around five days, four to five days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is a supplementary question for the bridging loan, specifically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have encountered companies which hire quite a number of Singaporean workers because they are unable to obtain the bridging loan from ESG, in particular, in this instance where the local shareholding and ownership of company is less than 30%.
